n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: A year to the day since you first walked through Ruth’s gate.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: I am getting old, {player}. One of these days I will hang up this hat for good.

deal.speaker: tendai
deal.text: Even with Hale’s men on our northern fence, I want to see this place the way Ruth dreamed it before I go.

lock.speaker: tendai
lock.text: Behind all this new wire, I still want to see this place the way Ruth dreamed it before I go.

free.speaker: tendai
free.text: With Hale gone, I want to see this place the way Ruth dreamed it before I go.

goal.speaker: tendai
goal.text: Every animal that belongs here. Every fence ours. And not one more animal lost to a snare.

n7.speaker: amara
n7.text: In numbers: all ten species living here, the ecosystem healthy for days on end, every zone open, a month without poaching, and a name people trust.

n8.speaker: narrator
n8.text: Max out your reserve: the goals are in the tracker. Any species that has died out can be bought back from the Species menu (K).

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Wanjiru comes up the east road on foot.

warm.speaker: wanjiru
warm.text: The council has a proposal. Our young people want to train as rangers. They know every path out there better than any truck driver.

n2.speaker: wanjiru
n2.text: Ruth always said the reserve needs the village and the village needs the reserve. I used to think she was being polite.

cool.speaker: wanjiru
cool.text: My grandson asks me what is behind your fence. I tell him: animals, and people who do not come to the village any more.

n4.speaker: wanjiru
n4.text: It is not too late to change that, {player}. But it is getting later.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: She stays for tea, and leaves before dark.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The post brings a letter in careful handwriting.

free.speaker: kito
free.text: My mother is well again. I have a job at the clinic in town. I tell the boys there what happens to people who carry snares.

n2.speaker: kito
n2.text: Tell Tendai the tea was terrible. And thank you.

jail.speaker: kito
jail.text: They let me go after the trial. I testified about the trucks. I am sorry for the snares. I hope the rhino is still there.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: Ten species. Grazers, browsers, hunters, scavengers. It is a whole ecosystem again, {player}. Look at it.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Ruth had a list of these on her office wall. I took it down when the last giraffe went. I think I will put it back up.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Fifteen days without a snare, a shot or a poisoned bird. I had forgotten what quiet sounds like.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: We are still missing some of the reserve’s species. If any have died out here, the Species menu (K) has offers from other reserves.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Some of the reserve is still behind broken fences. Mend them and every zone will be ours again.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: Ecosystem Health comes from three things: green grass, every species doing well, and water in every zone. Hover the leaf meter to see which one is holding us back.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Dusk at the tower. Everyone is here.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: I ran the numbers one more time this morning. I have never seen a reserve recover this fast. Never.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Ruth gave me this hat the day she hired me. Thirty-two years ago.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: It is yours now, {player}. It always was going to be. Ruth just did not live to hand it over.

choices.text: Thank you, Tendai. For staying, all those years.
Only if you promise not to retire just yet.

thanks.speaker: tendai
thanks.text: Somebody had to keep the gate shut.

stay.speaker: tendai
stay.text: Hm. Maybe one more season. Somebody has to keep you out of trouble.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: Below the tower, the herds move down to the water as the light goes.
